# From ski instructor to skipper: how I ended up at sea

URL: https://ivorbenko.com/blog/from-ski-instructor-to-skipper/
Author: Ivor Benko
Published: 2026-09-28
Language: en

Short answer: Ivor Benko is a Croatian skipper from Zagreb. He grew up skiing, became a licensed ISIA ski instructor, discovered sailing while studying at the Faculty of Kinesiology in Zagreb, and has worked as a skipper on sailboats and catamarans in the Adriatic since 2023.

People sometimes ask how someone from Zagreb, far from the sea, ends up as a skipper. For me it went through the mountains first.

## Skiing first

I've been skiing my whole life. It became more than a hobby, and I became a licensed ski instructor with an ISIA licence. Teaching skiing taught me something I still use every day on a boat: people relax and learn best when they trust the person in charge and are having fun at the same time.

## Kinesiology, and then the sea

I studied at the Faculty of Kinesiology at the University of Zagreb, where I specialised in sailing and water sports. That's where I discovered sailing, and I was hooked almost immediately.

What followed was a lot of time on the water:

- sailing small boat classes like the Laser Radial, Optimist and Laser Stratos
- windsurfing
- working as a sailing instructor for the Faculty of Kinesiology on Murter
- racing in regattas
- sailing big boats, 45 feet and up, all over the Adriatic

## Becoming a skipper

At some point the hobby became a profession. Since 2023 I've worked as a captain and skipper for private guests and charters, on monohulls like the Bénéteau First 45, Bavaria 46 and Dufour 46, and on catamarans like the Lagoon 42, Lagoon 450 and Lagoon 46.

In 2024 I completed the Sail Week skipper academy course with an A grade. I hold a Croatian boat licence (category C).

## What I bring on board

- **Knowledge of the Adriatic weather.** Reading bura, jugo and maestral is the core of the job. I wrote about it in [this guide to Adriatic winds](/blog/adriatic-winds-bura-jugo-maestral/).
- **More than ten years of organising sports activities**, from ski lessons to windsurfing, fitness and sailing. Keeping a group safe, busy and happy is familiar work.
- **Three languages.** Croatian is my mother tongue, I speak English at C1 level and German at B1.
- **A calm, cheerful way of working with people.** That matters as much as seamanship when you share a boat for a week.

## Beyond sailing

In winter I'm back on the slopes, and I also build websites and apps, including this one. This blog will focus on sailing for now, with skiing posts to follow.

If you're planning a week at sea in Croatia, [see how I work as a skipper](/skipper/) or [read more about me](/about/).

---

# What to pack for a week of sailing in Croatia

URL: https://ivorbenko.com/blog/what-to-pack-sailing-croatia/
Author: Ivor Benko
Published: 2026-09-21
Language: en

Short answer: Pack light in a soft bag, bring non-marking shoes, strong sun protection, a warm layer and a windproof jacket for the evenings, a power bank and your documents. Leave the hard suitcase and most of your wardrobe at home.

Storage space on a sailboat is limited, and the Croatian summer is simpler than people expect. This is the list I send to my guests.

## The bag

Bring a **soft bag**, not a hard suitcase. Hard suitcases don't fit into cabin lockers and there's nowhere to keep them. A duffel bag folds flat and disappears.

## Clothes

- swimwear, at least two sets, so one is always dry
- light shorts and T-shirts
- a long-sleeved shirt that blocks the sun
- **a warm layer** for the evenings, because it gets cool on the water, especially if bura blows
- **a light windproof and waterproof jacket**
- something nicer for dinner in town

That's enough. You'll wear far less than you pack.

## Shoes

- **deck shoes or trainers with light, non-marking soles**, because black soles leave marks on the deck
- sandals for towns
- water shoes if you like rocky beaches, since sea urchins are common on the rocks

## Sun and heat

The sun on the water is stronger than on land, because it also reflects off the sea.

- sunscreen with high protection, and plenty of it
- a hat that won't blow away, or one with a strap
- polarised sunglasses with a strap
- lip balm with SPF
- a refillable water bottle

## Health

- **seasickness remedies** if you're prone to it, taken before you sail, not after you feel ill
- your regular medicines, plasters and something for small cuts
- after-sun

## Electronics

- a power bank and USB cables; most boats have USB sockets, but there are never enough
- a waterproof phone pouch or a small **dry bag**
- a headlamp or small torch for evenings at anchor

## Documents and money

- ID card or passport for everyone
- your boat licence and VHF certificate, if you're sailing without a skipper
- a bank card, plus some cash for small konobas, bakeries and mooring buoys in smaller bays

## Nice to have

- snorkel and mask
- a quick-dry towel for the beach, though boats usually come with towels, so check with the charter company
- a book, cards or a small speaker at a considerate volume

## Leave at home

The hard suitcase, high heels, hair dryers (most boats can't power them away from the marina) and more than one "just in case" outfit.

If you're sailing with me, I'll send you a short list tailored to the boat and the season before you arrive. [Here's how I work as a skipper](/skipper/).

---

# Sailing the Kornati: a skipper's guide to the national park

URL: https://ivorbenko.com/blog/sailing-kornati-national-park/
Author: Ivor Benko
Published: 2026-09-14
Language: en

Short answer: The Kornati National Park is a maze of 89 islands, islets and reefs in central Dalmatia, and one of the best sailing areas in Croatia. Start from Murter or another nearby base, buy the park ticket before you enter, fill up water and fuel beforehand, and plan anchorages around the wind.

Kornati is where I spent a lot of my early time at sea. I worked as a sailing instructor on Murter, the island right next door, so these islands feel a little like home.

## What the Kornati are

The Kornati National Park was founded in 1980 and covers 89 islands, islets and reefs. The landscape is unlike anywhere else on the Croatian coast: bare, pale stone islands with almost no trees, dry-stone walls running across the hills, and very clear water. On the seaward side, many islands end in steep cliffs, locally called "krune" (crowns).

It is quiet. There are no towns inside the park, only a few seasonal houses and restaurants in the coves.

## Where to start

The closest bases are on Murter, including the villages of Murter, Jezera and Betina, all within a few hours of sailing. Charters from the Šibenik and Zadar areas also reach the Kornati easily, and Telašćica Nature Park on Dugi otok lies at the northwestern end of the archipelago.

## Before you enter the park

- **Buy the park ticket.** Every boat entering the park needs a ticket. It is sold online and at reception points, and it is usually cheaper to buy in advance than inside the park.
- **Fill up water and fuel.** There is very little of either inside the park. Leave with full tanks.
- **Know the rules.** Anchoring, fishing and diving are restricted in some zones, and there are strictly protected areas. The rules are published by the park and change from time to time, so check them before the trip.

## Weather in the Kornati

The islands are low and bare, so they offer little protection from the wind itself, only from the waves. That makes choosing the right cove for the night especially important:

- in maestral, pick coves open to the southeast and closed to the northwest
- in bura, pick coves protected to the northeast
- in jugo, avoid bays open to the south and southeast

I explain the three winds in more detail in [bura, jugo and maestral explained](/blog/adriatic-winds-bura-jugo-maestral/).

## How I like to sail the Kornati

A good Kornati day has no fixed plan. A morning swim in a still bay, a sail between the islands in the afternoon breeze, a walk up to a viewpoint above the cove, and dinner at one of the konobas where you can tie up if you eat there. Give the park at least one full day, ideally two, with a night anchored inside.

## Combine it with

- **Telašćica** and the saltwater lake Mir on Dugi otok
- the **Krka** river estuary and Skradin, if your base is near Šibenik
- the small islands of the Šibenik archipelago on the way back

If you'd like to sail the Kornati with someone who knows the area, [take a look at my skipper services](/skipper/).

---

# Catamaran or sailboat for a charter in Croatia?

URL: https://ivorbenko.com/blog/catamaran-or-sailboat-croatia/
Author: Ivor Benko
Published: 2026-09-09
Language: en

Short answer: Choose a catamaran if you want space, stability at anchor and comfort for a family or a larger group. Choose a monohull sailboat if you want the real feel of sailing, easier berths in busy marinas and a lower price. Both work well in the Adriatic.

I skipper both. Recently that has meant monohulls like the Bénéteau First 45, Bavaria 46 and Dufour 46, and catamarans like the Lagoon 42, Lagoon 450 and Lagoon 46. Guests often ask which one I'd choose. It depends on the group.

## Space and living on board

Catamarans win clearly here. The saloon and cockpit are on one level, the trampoline at the front becomes the most popular place on board, and the cabins are spread across two hulls, which gives more privacy.

On a monohull of 45 to 46 feet, living space is good, but everything is more compact and the cabins are closer together.

## Stability

A catamaran doesn't heel. That matters for people who get seasick, for families with small children and for anyone who wants to cook or read while sailing. At anchor, a catamaran rolls much less when a swell comes into the bay.

A monohull heels under sail. For many people that is exactly the fun of it, but some guests find it uncomfortable at first.

## The feel of sailing

If you want to feel the boat come alive, choose a monohull. It points higher into the wind, responds more directly to the helm and sails well in the moderate breezes that are typical of an Adriatic summer. A performance-oriented cruiser like the First 45 is a joy in a good maestral.

A cruising catamaran sails well off the wind, but it doesn't point as high, and in light air many charter catamarans end up motoring more.

## Marinas and anchorages

Monohulls fit into more marina berths and are simpler to moor stern-to. Catamarans are wide, so in peak season some marinas have limited space for them, and prices are often higher.

On the other hand, a catamaran's shallow draft means you can anchor closer to the beach in many bays.

## Cost

For a comparable size and season, a catamaran usually costs noticeably more to charter than a monohull. Fuel costs are also higher, because there are two engines.

## My recommendation

- **Families, larger groups, first-time sailors, people prone to seasickness:** catamaran.
- **Couples and friends who want to sail, smaller budgets, people who love the feeling of heel:** monohull.
- **Mixed groups:** a catamaran is the safer choice for keeping everyone happy.

Whichever you choose, the weather and the route matter more than the hull count. If you're not sure, [get in touch](/skipper/#contact) and I'll help you decide before you book.

---

# Bura, jugo and maestral: the Adriatic winds explained by a skipper

URL: https://ivorbenko.com/blog/adriatic-winds-bura-jugo-maestral/
Author: Ivor Benko
Published: 2026-09-04
Language: en

Short answer: Three winds shape sailing in Croatia. Maestral is the friendly northwesterly afternoon breeze of summer. Bura is a cold, gusty northeasterly that can arrive fast and strong. Jugo is a warm southeasterly that builds over a day or two and brings big waves. Skippers plan every route around which one is coming.

Every sailing week in Croatia is planned around one question: which wind is coming? Once you know the three main winds, the Adriatic becomes much easier to read.

## Maestral: the summer sailing wind

Maestral is a northwesterly thermal breeze. On a typical summer day the morning is calm, the breeze fills in around late morning or midday, peaks in the afternoon and dies down around sunset.

It is the wind most charter guests remember fondly: steady, predictable and usually moderate. It means fair weather. A classic summer routine is to motor or swim in the calm morning, sail in the maestral after lunch, and reach the evening anchorage before it drops.

## Bura: fast, cold and gusty

Bura (bora) blows from the northeast, down from the mountains along the coast towards the sea. It is dry and cold, and it often comes with a clear blue sky, which is exactly why it catches people out.

What makes bura dangerous is not only its strength but its gusts. It is gusty and uneven, and it is strongest in certain areas below the coastal mountains, such as the Velebit Channel. In summer it is usually shorter and weaker than in winter, but even a summer bura can make an exposed anchorage unusable within an hour.

Signs I watch for:

- a forecast for a northeasterly, even a "moderate" one
- a band of cloud sitting on the mountain tops along the coast, locally called a cap
- a sudden drop in temperature and very clear air

When bura is forecast, I choose anchorages and harbours protected to the north and east, and I don't plan open-water crossings under the mountains.

## Jugo: warm, wet and building

Jugo blows from the southeast. It is warm and humid, and it builds gradually, often over a day or two. It runs along the whole length of the Adriatic, so it has space to raise a long, heavy sea.

Jugo is more common outside the peak summer months, but it can appear in any season. It often brings haze, low cloud and rain. Signs:

- falling barometric pressure
- humid, heavy air and poor visibility
- swell from the southeast before the wind itself arrives

In jugo, bays open to the south and southeast become uncomfortable or dangerous, and crossing between islands against it is slow and wet.

## Other winds you'll hear about

- **Burin** is a light night breeze blowing from land to sea, the night-time counterpart to maestral.
- **Tramontana** comes from the north. It is cooler and can be strong.
- **Lebić (garbin)** comes from the southwest. It is less common but can be short and violent, and it hits harbours that are otherwise well protected.

## Which forecasts to use

I use the official forecasts of the Croatian Meteorological and Hydrological Service (DHMZ), including the maritime forecast and its model-based wind maps, and compare them with global apps. Coastal radio stations broadcast weather reports on VHF, and marina offices usually post the forecast every day.

The rule I work by is simple: check the forecast in the morning and in the evening, and choose tonight's anchorage for tomorrow's wind, not today's.

## Why this matters for your holiday

Knowing the winds is what lets a skipper keep a week both safe and enjoyable. It's the difference between being stuck in a rolling anchorage and waking up in a calm bay that the forecast said would be sheltered. If you'd like a skipper who plans around the weather, [here's how I work](/skipper/).

---

# Do you need a skipper for a sailing holiday in Croatia?

URL: https://ivorbenko.com/blog/do-you-need-a-skipper-croatia/
Author: Ivor Benko
Published: 2026-08-31
Language: en

Short answer: You need a skipper in Croatia if nobody in your group holds a boat licence recognised in Croatia plus a VHF radio certificate. Even with licences, many groups hire one to handle marinas, anchoring and weather, so that everyone else can actually be on holiday.

I get this question from almost every group that books a charter for the first time. The honest answer has two parts: what the rules say, and what the week will feel like.

## What the rules say

To take a charter yacht out without a professional, at least one person on board has to hold a boat licence recognised in Croatia, and in practice also a VHF radio operator certificate (often called SRC). Charter companies check both documents at check-in, before they hand over the boat.

If nobody in your group has them, you book the boat "with skipper". The charter company either assigns one or you bring your own, like me.

## What a skipper actually does

A skipper is responsible for the boat and for the safety of everyone on it. In a normal week that means:

- **Planning the route around the weather.** In the Adriatic, a good route is decided by the forecast, not by a list of famous places. I check it every morning and evening and adjust the plan.
- **Marinas, buoys and anchoring.** Mediterranean mooring (stern-to with lazy lines) in a busy marina in July is the most stressful part of most charters. That is my job.
- **Boat check-in and check-out.** Going through the inventory, the engine, the sails and the damage report with the charter base, so you are not surprised at the end of the week.
- **Local knowledge.** Which bays are protected from which wind, where you can tie up if you eat at the restaurant, where the water is clearest in the morning.
- **Teaching, if you want it.** Many guests want to steer, trim sails or learn to tie the essential knots. I worked as a sailing instructor, so I'm happy to turn the week into a course.

## What a skipper usually doesn't do

A skipper is not a cook or a cleaner. Some crews share cooking with the skipper, some eat out every night, but by default meal preparation and cleaning the guest cabins are not part of the job. If you want that, ask the charter company about a hostess.

## Even if you have a licence

A licence proves you passed an exam. It doesn't tell you how the maestral builds on a July afternoon near Split, or which anchorage will be uncomfortable if the wind turns overnight. Groups with a licensed friend often hire a skipper anyway, so that the friend can also have a holiday.

## What to agree on before the trip

- **Skipper fee and food.** The skipper's fee is usually paid separately from the boat, and guests normally cover the skipper's meals on board. Confirm both with the charter company or with the skipper directly.
- **Where the skipper sleeps.** Usually a separate cabin or the skipper's cabin that many catamarans have in the bow. Settle this before you choose the boat.
- **The rough plan.** Tell your skipper what you want: long sailing days, quiet anchorages, towns and nightlife, or a mix. A good skipper then builds the week around the weather.
- **Language.** Make sure you can communicate easily. I sail in Croatian, English and German.

## The short version

If you have no licence, you need a skipper. If you have one but want the week to feel like a holiday, a skipper is still the easiest upgrade you can make. If you're planning a charter in Croatia and would like me on board, [see how I work as a skipper](/skipper/).

---

# Od instruktora skijanja do skipera: kako sam završio na moru

URL: https://ivorbenko.com/hr/blog/od-instruktora-skijanja-do-skipera/
Author: Ivor Benko
Published: 2026-09-28
Language: hr

Short answer: Ivor Benko je hrvatski skiper iz Zagreba. Odrastao je na skijama, postao licencirani ISIA instruktor skijanja, jedrenje otkrio tijekom studija na Kineziološkom fakultetu u Zagrebu i od 2023. radi kao skiper na jedrilicama i katamaranima na Jadranu.

Ljudi me ponekad pitaju kako netko iz Zagreba, daleko od mora, postane skiper. Kod mene je put išao najprije preko planina.

## Najprije skijanje

Skijam cijeli život. To je postalo više od hobija i postao sam licencirani instruktor skijanja s ISIA licencom. Podučavanje skijanja naučilo me nečemu što i danas svaki dan koristim na brodu: ljudi se najbolje opuste i najviše nauče kad vjeruju osobi koja vodi i kad se pritom zabavljaju.

## Kineziologija, a onda more

Studirao sam na Kineziološkom fakultetu Sveučilišta u Zagrebu, gdje sam se usmjerio na jedrenje i sportove na vodi. Tamo sam otkrio jedrenje i gotovo odmah se zaljubio u njega.

Uslijedilo je puno vremena na vodi:

- jedrenje u malim klasama poput Laser Radiala, Optimista i Laser Stratosa
- windsurfing
- rad kao instruktor jedrenja za Kineziološki fakultet na Murteru
- regate
- jedrenje na velikim brodovima, od 45 stopa naviše, po cijelom Jadranu

## Kako sam postao skiper

U jednom trenutku hobi je postao posao. Od 2023. radim kao kapetan i skiper za privatne goste i chartere, na jedrilicama poput Bénéteau First 45, Bavaria 46 i Dufour 46 te na katamaranima poput Lagoon 42, Lagoon 450 i Lagoon 46.

Godine 2024. završio sam Sail Week skipersku akademiju s ocjenom A. Imam ispit za voditelja brodice kategorije C.

## Što donosim na brod

- **Poznavanje jadranskog vremena.** Čitanje bure, juga i maestrala srž je posla. O tome sam pisao u [vodiču kroz jadranske vjetrove](/hr/blog/bura-jugo-maestral-vjetrovi-jadran/).
- **Više od deset godina organiziranja sportskih aktivnosti**, od škole skijanja do windsurfinga, fitnessa i jedrenja. Grupu držati sigurnom, zaposlenom i zadovoljnom poznat mi je posao.
- **Tri jezika.** Hrvatski mi je materinski, engleski govorim na razini C1, a njemački na razini B1.
- **Smiren i vedar način rada s ljudima.** To je jednako važno kao pomorsko znanje kad tjedan dana dijelite brod.

## Osim jedrenja

Zimi sam opet na skijalištu, a izrađujem i web stranice i aplikacije, uključujući i ovu. Blog će se za sada baviti jedrenjem, a tekstovi o skijanju slijede.

Ako planirate tjedan na moru u Hrvatskoj, [pogledajte kako radim kao skiper](/hr/skiper/) ili [pročitajte više o meni](/hr/o-meni/).

---

# Što ponijeti na tjedan jedrenja u Hrvatskoj

URL: https://ivorbenko.com/hr/blog/sto-ponijeti-na-jedrenje/
Author: Ivor Benko
Published: 2026-09-21
Language: hr

Short answer: Pakirajte lagano u mekanu torbu, ponesite obuću sa svijetlim đonom, jaku zaštitu od sunca, topliji sloj i vjetrovku za večeri, powerbank i dokumente. Tvrdi kofer i veći dio ormara ostavite kod kuće.

Prostor za stvari na jedrilici je ograničen, a hrvatsko ljeto jednostavnije je nego što ljudi očekuju. Ovo je popis koji šaljem svojim gostima.

## Torba

Ponesite **mekanu torbu**, ne tvrdi kofer. Tvrdi koferi ne stanu u ormariće u kabini i nemate ih gdje odložiti. Putna torba se složi i nestane.

## Odjeća

- kupaći, barem dva, da je jedan uvijek suh
- lagane kratke hlače i majice
- košulja dugih rukava koja štiti od sunca
- **topliji sloj** za večeri, jer na moru zna zahladiti, posebno ako puše bura
- **lagana jakna koja ne propušta vjetar i vodu**
- nešto urednije za večeru u gradu

To je dovoljno. Nosit ćete puno manje nego što spakirate.

## Obuća

- **brodske cipele ili tenisice sa svijetlim đonom koji ne ostavlja tragove**, jer crni đon ostavlja tragove na palubi
- sandale za grad
- obuća za more ako volite stjenovite plaže, jer su ježinci česti na kamenju

## Sunce i vrućina

Sunce na moru jače je nego na kopnu jer se odbija i od površine mora.

- krema s visokim zaštitnim faktorom, i to puno
- šešir koji neće odletjeti, ili onaj s trakom
- polarizirane sunčane naočale s vezicom
- balzam za usne sa SPF-om
- boca za vodu za višekratnu upotrebu

## Zdravlje

- **sredstvo protiv morske bolesti** ako ste skloni, uzeto prije isplovljavanja, a ne kad vam već bude loše
- vaši redoviti lijekovi, flasteri i nešto za manje posjekotine
- losion poslije sunčanja

## Elektronika

- powerbank i USB kabeli; većina brodova ima USB utičnice, ali nikad ih nema dovoljno
- vodootporna futrola za mobitel ili mala **vodootporna vreća**
- čeona ili mala ručna svjetiljka za večeri na sidru

## Dokumenti i novac

- osobna iskaznica ili putovnica za svakoga
- ispit za voditelja brodice i VHF svjedodžba, ako jedrite bez skipera
- kartica i nešto gotovine za male konobe, pekare i bove u manjim uvalama

## Dobro je imati

- masku i dihalicu
- ručnik za plažu koji se brzo suši, iako brodovi obično imaju ručnike, pa provjerite s charter tvrtkom
- knjigu, karte ili mali zvučnik na pristojnoj glasnoći

## Ostavite kod kuće

Tvrdi kofer, visoke pete, sušilo za kosu (većina brodova ga ne može pokrenuti izvan marine) i više od jedne odjevne kombinacije "za svaki slučaj".

Ako jedrite sa mnom, prije dolaska poslat ću vam kratak popis prilagođen brodu i dijelu sezone. [Pogledajte kako radim kao skiper](/hr/skiper/).

---

# Jedrenje po Kornatima: skiperski vodič kroz nacionalni park

URL: https://ivorbenko.com/hr/blog/jedrenje-kornati-nacionalni-park/
Author: Ivor Benko
Published: 2026-09-14
Language: hr

Short answer: Nacionalni park Kornati labirint je od 89 otoka, otočića i hridi u srednjoj Dalmaciji i jedno od najljepših područja za jedrenje u Hrvatskoj. Krenite s Murtera ili obližnje baze, kupite ulaznicu za park prije ulaska, napunite vodu i gorivo i birajte sidrišta prema vjetru.

Na Kornatima sam proveo puno svog ranog vremena na moru. Radio sam kao instruktor jedrenja na Murteru, otoku odmah do njih, pa mi se ovi otoci čine pomalo kao dom.

## Što su Kornati

Nacionalni park Kornati osnovan je 1980. i obuhvaća 89 otoka, otočića i hridi. Krajolik ne liči ni na što drugo na hrvatskoj obali: goli, svijetli kameni otoci gotovo bez drveća, suhozidi preko brda i vrlo bistro more. S pučinske strane mnogi otoci završavaju strmim liticama koje se zovu krune.

Tiho je. U parku nema naselja, samo nekoliko sezonskih kuća i konoba u uvalama.

## Odakle krenuti

Najbliže baze su na Murteru, u mjestima Murter, Jezera i Betina, sve na nekoliko sati jedrenja. Do Kornata se lako stiže i s charterom iz šibenskog i zadarskog područja, a Park prirode Telašćica na Dugom otoku nalazi se na sjeverozapadnom kraju arhipelaga.

## Prije ulaska u park

- **Kupite ulaznicu.** Svaki brod koji ulazi u park treba ulaznicu. Prodaje se online i na prodajnim mjestima, a obično je jeftinija ako je kupite unaprijed nego u parku.
- **Napunite vodu i gorivo.** Unutar parka nema ni jednog ni drugog u značajnijoj mjeri. Isplovite s punim tankovima.
- **Upoznajte pravila.** Sidrenje, ribolov i ronjenje ograničeni su u nekim zonama, a postoje i strogo zaštićena područja. Pravila objavljuje park i povremeno se mijenjaju, pa ih provjerite prije puta.

## Vrijeme na Kornatima

Otoci su niski i goli, pa slabo štite od samog vjetra, samo od valova. Zato je izbor prave uvale za noć posebno važan:

- po maestralu birajte uvale otvorene prema jugoistoku, a zatvorene prema sjeverozapadu
- po buri birajte uvale zaštićene sa sjeveroistoka
- po jugu izbjegavajte uvale otvorene prema jugu i jugoistoku

Tri vjetra detaljnije objašnjavam u tekstu [bura, jugo i maestral](/hr/blog/bura-jugo-maestral-vjetrovi-jadran/).

## Kako ja volim jedriti po Kornatima

Dobar dan na Kornatima nema čvrst plan. Jutarnje kupanje u mirnoj uvali, jedrenje među otocima u poslijepodnevnom vjetru, šetnja do vidikovca iznad uvale i večera u nekoj od konoba gdje se možete vezati ako jedete kod njih. Parku dajte barem jedan cijeli dan, idealno dva, s noćenjem na sidru unutra.

## Kombinirajte s

- **Telašćicom** i slanim jezerom Mir na Dugom otoku
- ušćem **Krke** i Skradinom, ako vam je baza kod Šibenika
- malim otocima šibenskog arhipelaga na povratku

Ako želite jedriti po Kornatima s nekim tko poznaje područje, [pogledajte moje skiperske usluge](/hr/skiper/).

---

# Katamaran ili jedrilica za charter u Hrvatskoj?

URL: https://ivorbenko.com/hr/blog/katamaran-ili-jedrilica/
Author: Ivor Benko
Published: 2026-09-09
Language: hr

Short answer: Katamaran birajte ako želite prostor, stabilnost na sidru i udobnost za obitelj ili veću grupu. Jednotrupnu jedrilicu birajte ako želite pravi osjećaj jedrenja, lakši vez u punim marinama i nižu cijenu. Oboje odlično funkcionira na Jadranu.

Vozim i jedno i drugo. U posljednje vrijeme to su jednotrupne jedrilice poput Bénéteau First 45, Bavaria 46 i Dufour 46 te katamarani poput Lagoon 42, Lagoon 450 i Lagoon 46. Gosti me često pitaju što bih ja izabrao. Ovisi o grupi.

## Prostor i život na brodu

Ovdje katamaran jasno pobjeđuje. Salon i kokpit su na istoj razini, trampolin na pramcu postaje najpopularnije mjesto na brodu, a kabine su raspoređene u dva trupa, što daje više privatnosti.

Na jedrilici od 45 do 46 stopa prostora ima dovoljno, ali sve je kompaktnije i kabine su bliže jedna drugoj.

## Stabilnost

Katamaran se ne naginje. To je važno onima koje hvata morska bolest, obiteljima s malom djecom i svima koji žele kuhati ili čitati tijekom plovidbe. Na sidru se katamaran puno manje ljulja kad u uvalu uđe mrtvo more.

Jedrilica se pod jedrima naginje. Mnogima je upravo to najveći užitak, ali nekim gostima isprva nije ugodno.

## Osjećaj jedrenja

Ako želite osjetiti kako brod oživi, birajte jedrilicu. Oštrije ide u vjetar, izravnije reagira na kormilo i dobro jedri u umjerenom vjetru tipičnom za jadransko ljeto. Brza krstarica poput Firsta 45 pravi je užitak u dobrom maestralu.

Krstareći katamaran dobro jedri u niz vjetar, ali ne ide tako oštro, a u slabom vjetru mnogi charter katamarani na kraju više idu na motor.

## Marine i sidrišta

Jedrilice stanu u više vezova u marinama i jednostavnije se vežu krmom. Katamarani su široki, pa u sezoni neke marine imaju ograničen prostor za njih, a cijene su često više.

S druge strane, zbog malog gaza katamaranom se u mnogim uvalama možete usidriti bliže plaži.

## Cijena

Za usporedivu veličinu i termin najam katamarana obično je osjetno skuplji od jedrilice. Potrošnja goriva također je veća jer ima dva motora.

## Moja preporuka

- **Obitelji, veće grupe, početnici, osobe sklone morskoj bolesti:** katamaran.
- **Parovi i prijatelji koji žele jedriti, manji budžet, oni koji vole nagib:** jedrilica.
- **Mješovite grupe:** katamaran je sigurniji izbor da svi budu zadovoljni.

Što god izabrali, vrijeme i ruta važniji su od broja trupova. Ako niste sigurni, [javite mi se](/hr/skiper/#kontakt) i pomoći ću vam odlučiti prije rezervacije.

---

# Bura, jugo i maestral: jadranski vjetrovi iz perspektive skipera

URL: https://ivorbenko.com/hr/blog/bura-jugo-maestral-vjetrovi-jadran/
Author: Ivor Benko
Published: 2026-09-04
Language: hr

Short answer: Jedrenje u Hrvatskoj oblikuju tri vjetra. Maestral je ugodan ljetni sjeverozapadnjak koji puše poslijepodne. Bura je hladan, refulast sjeveroistočnjak koji može doći brzo i jako. Jugo je topli jugoistočnjak koji se diže dan ili dva i donosi velike valove. Skiperi svaku rutu planiraju prema tome koji dolazi.

Svaki tjedan jedrenja u Hrvatskoj planira se oko jednog pitanja: koji vjetar dolazi? Kad upoznate tri glavna vjetra, Jadran postaje puno lakše čitati.

## Maestral: ljetni vjetar za jedrenje

Maestral je termički vjetar sa sjeverozapada. U tipičnom ljetnom danu jutro je mirno, vjetar se diže krajem jutra ili oko podneva, najjači je poslijepodne i smiruje se oko zalaska sunca.

To je vjetar koji gosti chartera najradije pamte: stalan, predvidljiv i najčešće umjeren. Znači lijepo vrijeme. Klasična ljetna rutina je motorom ili kupanjem kroz mirno jutro, jedrenje u maestralu nakon ručka i dolazak u večernje sidrište prije nego što stane.

## Bura: brza, hladna i refulasta

Bura puše sa sjeveroistoka, s planina uz obalu prema moru. Suha je i hladna, a često dolazi uz vedro plavo nebo, zbog čega mnoge i iznenadi.

Buru ne čini opasnom samo jačina nego i refuli. Puše na mahove i neravnomjerno, a najjača je u određenim područjima ispod obalnih planina, primjerice u Velebitskom kanalu. Ljeti je obično kraća i slabija nego zimi, ali i ljetna bura može u roku od sat vremena učiniti izloženo sidrište neupotrebljivim.

Znakovi na koje pazim:

- prognoza sjeveroistočnjaka, čak i "umjerenog"
- oblak koji sjedi na vrhovima obalnih planina, tzv. kapa
- nagli pad temperature i vrlo proziran zrak

Kad je najavljena bura, biram sidrišta i luke zaštićene sa sjevera i istoka i ne planiram prijelaze otvorenim morem ispod planina.

## Jugo: toplo, vlažno i postupno

Jugo puše s jugoistoka. Topao je i vlažan i diže se postupno, često dan ili dva. Puše duž cijelog Jadrana, pa ima prostora podići dugo i teško more.

Jugo je češći izvan vrhunca ljeta, ali se može pojaviti u bilo koje doba godine. Često donosi sumaglicu, nisku naoblaku i kišu. Znakovi:

- pad tlaka zraka
- vlažan, težak zrak i slaba vidljivost
- mrtvo more s jugoistoka i prije nego što vjetar stigne

Po jugu su uvale otvorene prema jugu i jugoistoku neugodne ili opasne, a plovidba između otoka protiv juga spora je i mokra.

## Ostali vjetrovi za koje ćete čuti

- **Burin** je slab noćni vjetar s kopna prema moru, noćni par maestralu.
- **Tramontana** puše sa sjevera. Hladnija je i može biti jaka.
- **Lebić (garbin)** puše s jugozapada. Rjeđi je, ali može biti kratak i silovit te pogađa luke koje su inače dobro zaštićene.

## Koje prognoze koristiti

Koristim službene prognoze Državnog hidrometeorološkog zavoda (DHMZ), uključujući pomorsku prognozu i karte vjetra iz modela, i uspoređujem ih s globalnim aplikacijama. Obalne radiostanice emitiraju vremenska izvješća na VHF-u, a marine obično svaki dan izvjese prognozu.

Pravilo po kojem radim je jednostavno: prognozu provjeri ujutro i navečer, a večerašnje sidrište biraj prema sutrašnjem vjetru, ne današnjem.

## Zašto je to važno za vaš odmor

Poznavanje vjetrova skiperu omogućuje da tjedan bude i siguran i ugodan. To je razlika između noći u sidrištu koje ljulja i buđenja u mirnoj uvali za koju je prognoza rekla da će biti zaštićena. Ako želite skipera koji planira prema vremenu, [pogledajte kako radim](/hr/skiper/).

---

# Treba li vam skiper za jedrenje u Hrvatskoj?

URL: https://ivorbenko.com/hr/blog/treba-li-mi-skiper/
Author: Ivor Benko
Published: 2026-08-31
Language: hr

Short answer: Skiper vam treba ako nitko u vašoj grupi nema ispit za voditelja brodice priznat u Hrvatskoj i svjedodžbu za VHF radio. I s ispitom mnoge ga grupe unajme da vodi marine, sidrenje i vrijeme, kako bi svi ostali zaista bili na odmoru.

Ovo pitanje dobijem od gotovo svake grupe koja prvi put unajmljuje brod. Iskren odgovor ima dva dijela: što kažu propisi i kako će tjedan izgledati u praksi.

## Što kažu propisi

Da biste charter brod vodili sami, bez profesionalca, barem jedna osoba na brodu mora imati ispit za voditelja brodice priznat u Hrvatskoj, a u praksi i svjedodžbu za VHF radiotelefoniju (SRC). Charter tvrtke provjeravaju oba dokumenta pri preuzimanju broda.

Ako ih nitko u grupi nema, brod se rezervira "sa skiperom". Charter tvrtka ga dodijeli ili dovedete svog, primjerice mene.

## Što skiper zapravo radi

Skiper je odgovoran za brod i za sigurnost svih na njemu. U običnom tjednu to znači:

- **Planiranje rute prema vremenu.** Na Jadranu dobru rutu određuje prognoza, a ne popis poznatih mjesta. Provjeravam je svako jutro i večer i prilagođavam plan.
- **Marine, bove i sidrenje.** Vezivanje krmom uz mooring u punoj marini u srpnju najstresniji je dio većine chartera. To je moj posao.
- **Preuzimanje i predaja broda.** Prolazak kroz inventar, motor, jedra i zapisnik o oštećenjima s charter bazom, da vas na kraju tjedna ništa ne iznenadi.
- **Lokalno znanje.** Koje su uvale zaštićene od kojeg vjetra, gdje se možete vezati ako večerate u konobi, gdje je more najbistrije ujutro.
- **Učenje, ako želite.** Mnogi gosti žele kormilariti, trimati jedra ili naučiti osnovne čvorove. Radio sam kao instruktor jedrenja, pa rado pretvorim tjedan u tečaj.

## Što skiper obično ne radi

Skiper nije kuhar ni čistač. Neke posade kuhaju zajedno sa skiperom, neke svaku večer jedu vani, ali priprema obroka i čišćenje kabina gostiju nisu dio posla. Ako to želite, pitajte charter tvrtku za hostesu.

## Čak i ako imate ispit

Ispit dokazuje da ste položili ispit. Ne govori vam kako se maestral diže u srpanjsko poslijepodne kod Splita ni koje će sidrište postati neugodno ako vjetar noću okrene. Grupe s prijateljem koji ima ispit često ipak unajme skipera, da i taj prijatelj bude na odmoru.

## Što dogovoriti prije puta

- **Cijena skipera i hrana.** Skiper se obično plaća odvojeno od najma broda, a gosti u pravilu pokrivaju skiperove obroke na brodu. Potvrdite oboje s charter tvrtkom ili izravno sa skiperom.
- **Gdje skiper spava.** Najčešće u zasebnoj kabini ili u skiperskoj kabini koju mnogi katamarani imaju u pramcu. Dogovorite to prije odabira broda.
- **Okvirni plan.** Recite skiperu što želite: duge dane jedrenja, mirna sidrišta, gradove i izlaske ili kombinaciju. Dobar skiper onda slaže tjedan prema vremenu.
- **Jezik.** Provjerite da se lako sporazumijevate. Ja jedrim na hrvatskom, engleskom i njemačkom.

## Ukratko

Ako nemate ispit, treba vam skiper. Ako ga imate, a želite da tjedan bude pravi odmor, skiper je i dalje najlakša nadogradnja. Ako planirate charter u Hrvatskoj i želite mene na brodu, [pogledajte kako radim kao skiper](/hr/skiper/).

---
